title: The 1% Signal: How to Stand Out When AI Makes Everything Average

scenes.narration: When everyone on earth gets access to the exact same tools, average output drops to zero value. Every minute, an endless conveyor belt stamps out millions of identical grey clones.
We are entering an era of infinite supply. Generic essays, generic code, generic designs—when supply goes to infinity, the price of average collapses straight to zero.
Yet abundance of noise creates an extreme shortage of signal. People are desperate for a filter that rejects ninety-nine percent of filler and isolates the rare one percent that actually matters.
That filter is human taste. Knowing what to cut, what to emphasize, and what feels unmistakably real cannot be automated by pressing a single button.
Tools can generate ten thousand variations in seconds. Only a sharp mind with clear standards can tune jagged static into a clean, unforgettable signal.
In a world flooded with synthetic copies, a distinct point of view becomes a rare diamond. People do not follow perfection—they follow clarity, conviction, and original angles.
Your lived scars, your weird obsessions, your real-world experiments—those are the human signature that no generic template will ever replicate.
Do not compete with machines at being average. Use the tools for speed, sharpen your judgment—because when average becomes free, taste becomes priceless.
